The radius of a right circular cylinder is increasing at the rate of 333 cm/s and its height is decreasing at the rate of 444 cm/s. The rate of change of its volume when the radius is 444 cm and the height is 666 cm is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Both rrr and hhh change with ttt, so use the product rule on V=πr2hV = \pi r^2 hV=πr2h.

  1. 1

    Differentiate V=πr2hV = \pi r^2 hV=πr2h w.r.t. ttt (product rule)

    dVdt=π(2rh drdt+r2 dhdt)\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \pi\left(2rh\,\dfrac{dr}{dt} + r^2\,\dfrac{dh}{dt}\right)dtdV​=π(2rhdtdr​+r2dtdh​)dVdt=π(2rh drdt+r2 dhdt)\displaystyle \dfrac{dV}{dt} = \pi\left(2rh\,\dfrac{dr}{dt} + r^2\,\dfrac{dh}{dt}\right)dtdV​=π(2rhdtdr​+r2dtdh​)
  2. 2

    Put r=4r = 4r=4, h=6h = 6h=6, drdt=3\dfrac{dr}{dt} = 3dtdr​=3, dhdt=−4\dfrac{dh}{dt} = -4dtdh​=−4

    dVdt=π(2(4)(6)(3)+16(−4))=π(144−64)=80π\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \pi\big(2(4)(6)(3) + 16(-4)\big) = \pi(144 - 64) = 80\pidtdV​=π(2(4)(6)(3)+16(−4))=π(144−64)=80πdVdt=π(2(4)(6)(3)+16(−4))=π(144−64)=80π\displaystyle \dfrac{dV}{dt} = \pi\big(2(4)(6)(3) + 16(-4)\big) = \pi(144 - 64) = 80\pidtdV​=π(2(4)(6)(3)+16(−4))=π(144−64)=80π

    Height is decreasing, so dhdt\dfrac{dh}{dt}dtdh​ is negative

    1
Answer(A) 80π cm3/s\displaystyle 80\pi\ \text{cm}^3/\text{s}80π cm3/s

Watch out Taking dhdt=+4\dfrac{dh}{dt} = +4dtdh​=+4 gives 208π208\pi208π; dropping the hhh-term gives 144π144\pi144π.

At x=5π6x = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}x=65π​, f(x)=2sin⁡3x+3cos⁡3xf(x) = 2\sin 3x + 3\cos 3xf(x)=2sin3x+3cos3x is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea A local maximum or minimum of a differentiable function needs f′(c)=0f'(c) = 0f′(c)=0.

  1. 1

    Value at x=5π6x = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}x=65π​ (3x=5π23x = \dfrac{5\pi}{2}3x=25π​)

    f(5π6)=2sin⁡5π2+3cos⁡5π2=2(1)+0=2≠0f\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right) = 2\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{2} + 3\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{2} = 2(1) + 0 = 2 \neq 0f(65π​)=2sin25π​+3cos25π​=2(1)+0=2=0f(5π6)=2sin⁡5π2+3cos⁡5π2=2(1)+0=2≠0\displaystyle f\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right) = 2\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{2} + 3\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{2} = 2(1) + 0 = 2 \neq 0f(65π​)=2sin25π​+3cos25π​=2(1)+0=2=0
  2. 2

    Differentiate

    f′(x)=6cos⁡3x−9sin⁡3xf'(x) = 6\cos 3x - 9\sin 3xf′(x)=6cos3x−9sin3x
  3. 3

    f′(5π6)≠0f'\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right) \neq 0f′(65π​)=0, so it is not a point of extremum

    f′(5π6)=6(0)−9(1)=−9≠0f'\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right) = 6(0) - 9(1) = -9 \neq 0f′(65π​)=6(0)−9(1)=−9=0f′(5π6)=6(0)−9(1)=−9≠0\displaystyle f'\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right) = 6(0) - 9(1) = -9 \neq 0f′(65π​)=6(0)−9(1)=−9=0
    1
Answer(D) neither maximum nor minimum

Watch out Taking sin⁡3x=1\sin 3x = 1sin3x=1 as a sign of a maximum; the maximum of fff is 13\sqrt{13}13​, not 222.

Assertion (A): f(x)=x3f(x) = x^3f(x)=x3 is strictly increasing on R\mathbb{R}R. Reason (R): If a function fff is strictly increasing on an interval, then f′(x)>0f'(x) > 0f′(x)>0 for every xxx in that interval.

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea f′>0f' > 0f′>0 on an interval implies strictly increasing, but the converse is false.

  1. 1

    f′(x)=3x2>0f'(x) = 3x^2 > 0f′(x)=3x2>0 except at x=0x = 0x=0, so fff is strictly increasing: A is true

    x1<x2  ⇒  x13<x23x_1 < x_2 \;\Rightarrow\; x_1^3 < x_2^3x1​<x2​⇒x13​<x23​x1<x2  ⇒  x13<x23\displaystyle x_1 < x_2 \;\Rightarrow\; x_1^3 < x_2^3x1​<x2​⇒x13​<x23​
  2. 2

    x3x^3x3 is strictly increasing, yet f′(0)=0f'(0) = 0f′(0)=0: R is false

    f′(0)=3(0)2=0f'(0) = 3(0)^2 = 0f′(0)=3(0)2=0
  3. 3

    A is true and R is false

    Option (C)\text{Option (C)}Option (C)
    1
Answer(C) A is true, but R is false.

Watch out Choosing (A): R is the converse of the theorem, and x3x^3x3 is the counter-example.

The volume of a cube is increasing at the rate of 8 cm3/s8\ \text{cm}^3/\text{s}8 cm3/s. How fast is the surface area increasing when the length of an edge is 121212 cm?

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Find dxdt\dfrac{dx}{dt}dtdx​ from VVV, then use it in dSdt\dfrac{dS}{dt}dtdS​.

  1. 1

    Let edge =x= x=x; volume and surface area

    V=x3,S=6x2V = x^3,\qquad S = 6x^2V=x3,S=6x2
    ½
  2. 2

    Differentiate VVV w.r.t. ttt and use dVdt=8\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 8dtdV​=8

    3x2 dxdt=8  ⇒  dxdt=83x23x^2\,\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 8 \;\Rightarrow\; \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{8}{3x^2}3x2dtdx​=8⇒dtdx​=3x28​3x2 dxdt=8  ⇒  dxdt=83x2\displaystyle 3x^2\,\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 8 \;\Rightarrow\; \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{8}{3x^2}3x2dtdx​=8⇒dtdx​=3x28​
    ½
  3. 3

    Differentiate SSS w.r.t. ttt

    dSdt=12x dxdt=12x⋅83x2=32x\dfrac{dS}{dt} = 12x\,\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 12x\cdot\dfrac{8}{3x^2} = \dfrac{32}{x}dtdS​=12xdtdx​=12x⋅3x28​=x32​dSdt=12x dxdt=12x⋅83x2=32x\displaystyle \dfrac{dS}{dt} = 12x\,\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 12x\cdot\dfrac{8}{3x^2} = \dfrac{32}{x}dtdS​=12xdtdx​=12x⋅3x28​=x32​
    ½
  4. 4

    Put x=12x = 12x=12

    dSdt=3212=83 cm2/s\dfrac{dS}{dt} = \dfrac{32}{12} = \dfrac{8}{3}\ \text{cm}^2/\text{s}dtdS​=1232​=38​ cm2/sdSdt=3212=83 cm2/s\displaystyle \dfrac{dS}{dt} = \dfrac{32}{12} = \dfrac{8}{3}\ \text{cm}^2/\text{s}dtdS​=1232​=38​ cm2/s
    ½
AnswerSurface area increases at 83 cm2/s\displaystyle \dfrac{8}{3}\ \text{cm}^2/\text{s}38​ cm2/s

Watch out Using dxdt=8\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 8dtdx​=8; the 888 is the rate of change of volume, not of the edge.

Find the points of local maxima, local minima and the points of inflexion (critical points where f′f'f′ does not change sign) of the function f(x)=x5−5x4+5x3−1f(x) = x^5 - 5x^4 + 5x^3 - 1f(x)=x5−5x4+5x3−1. Also find the corresponding local maximum and local minimum values.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea First derivative test: f′f'f′ from +++ to −-− is a maximum; no sign change is a point of inflexion.

  1. 1

    Differentiate and factorise

    f′(x)=5x4−20x3+15x2=5x2(x−1)(x−3)f'(x) = 5x^4 - 20x^3 + 15x^2 = 5x^2(x - 1)(x - 3)f′(x)=5x4−20x3+15x2=5x2(x−1)(x−3)f′(x)=5x4−20x3+15x2=5x2(x−1)(x−3)\displaystyle f'(x) = 5x^4 - 20x^3 + 15x^2 = 5x^2(x - 1)(x - 3)f′(x)=5x4−20x3+15x2=5x2(x−1)(x−3)
    ½
  2. 2

    f′(x)=0f'(x) = 0f′(x)=0 gives

    x=0, 1, 3x = 0,\ 1,\ 3x=0, 1, 3
    ½
  3. 3

    Near x=0x = 0x=0, f′>0f' > 0f′>0 on both sides: no sign change

    x=0 is a point of inflexionx = 0 \text{ is a point of inflexion}x=0 is a point of inflexion

A wire of length 282828 m is to be cut into two pieces. One of the pieces is to be made into a square and the other into a circle. What should be the length of the two pieces so that the combined area of the square and the circle is minimum?

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Write the total area in one variable using 4a+2πr=284a + 2\pi r = 284a+2πr=28; minimum needs A′=0A' = 0A′=0, A′′>0A'' > 0A′′>0.

    ½

    Differentiate w.r.t. rrr

    dAdr=2(7−πr2)(−π2)+2πr=−7π+π2r2+2πr\dfrac{dA}{dr} = 2\left(7 - \dfrac{\pi r}{2}\right)\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) + 2\pi r = -7\pi + \dfrac{\pi^2 r}{2} + 2\pi rdrdA​=2(7−2πr​)(−2π​)+2πr=−7π+2π2r​+2πrdAdr=2(7−πr2)(−π2)+2πr=−7π+π2r2+2πr\displaystyle \dfrac{dA}{dr} = 2\left(7 - \dfrac{\pi r}{2}\right)\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) + 2\pi r = -7\pi + \dfrac{\pi^2 r}{2} + 2\pi rdrdA​=2(7−2πr​)(−2π​)+2πr=−7π+2π2r​+2πr
    1
  4. 4

    Put dAdr=0\dfrac{dA}{dr} = 0drdA​=0 and divide by π\piπ

    πr2+2r=7  ⇒  r=14π+4\dfrac{\pi r}{2} + 2r = 7 \;\Rightarrow\; r = \dfrac{14}{\pi + 4}2πr​+2r=7⇒r=π+414​πr2+2r=7  ⇒  r=14π+4\displaystyle \dfrac{\pi r}{2} + 2r = 7 \;\Rightarrow\; r = \dfrac{14}{\pi + 4}2πr​+2r=7⇒r=π+414​
    ½
  5. 5

    Second derivative test

    d2Adr2=π22+2π>0\dfrac{d^2A}{dr^2} = \dfrac{\pi^2}{2} + 2\pi > 0dr2d2A​=2π2​+2π>0d2Adr2=π22+2π>0\displaystyle \dfrac{d^2A}{dr^2} = \dfrac{\pi^2}{2} + 2\pi > 0dr2d2A​=2π2​+2π>0
    1
  6. 6

    So AAA is minimum; lengths of the two pieces

    circle: 2πr=28ππ+4 msquare: 28−28ππ+4=112π+4 m\begin{aligned} \text{circle: } 2\pi r &= \dfrac{28\pi}{\pi + 4}\ \text{m} \\ \text{square: } 28 - \dfrac{28\pi}{\pi + 4} &= \dfrac{112}{\pi + 4}\ \text{m} \end{aligned}circle: 2πrsquare: 28−π+428π​​=π+428π​ m=π+4112​ m​
    1
AnswerSquare piece =112π+4\displaystyle = \dfrac{112}{\pi + 4}=π+4112​ m and circle piece =28ππ+4\displaystyle = \dfrac{28\pi}{\pi + 4}=π+428π​ m
